dedupe_keys.name: critical infrastructure interdependency analysis operationalising resilience strategies gar 2019 contributing paper

description: This 33-page working paper proposes a framework for critical infrastructure interdependency analysis that combines top-down system-level and bottom-up asset-level analysis to show potential cascading and escalating failures and to prioritise resilience measures. Lawrence Paul Lewis and Frédéric Petit wrote it as a contributing paper to the 2019 Global Assessment Report on Disaster Risk Reduction, published by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, and they illustrate the framework with Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. The paper argues for using interdependency analysis in all phases of risk and emergency management and in long-term adaptation planning. Coverage is general, with a Puerto Rico illustration. Format and access: a free PDF from the UNDRR publication page. Licence: not stated on the page read; free. Caveats: it is a method paper, not a dataset, and the Puerto Rico results were not read in detail here. It guides the structure of cascading failure and resilience studies across sectors. Related catalogue records are Argonne's 2015 report on analysing infrastructure dependencies, by the same group, and the GAO review of telecommunications restoration after Hurricane Maria.
